stem: A team is finalizing the primary IPv4 CIDR block for a new VPC before any subnets exist. They expect to need roughly 40,000 addresses of headroom for future subnets, want to stay inside the CIDR block size AWS allows for a VPC, and want to draw from the address range AWS recommends for a VPC.
rationale: A /16 netmask gives 65,536 addresses, sits at the largest end of the /16-to-/28 range AWS allows for a VPC's CIDR block, and 10.0.0.0/16 falls inside the RFC 1918 private range AWS recommends. A /8 netmask is far larger than the /16 maximum AWS allows for a VPC block, so it cannot be used even though it would supply more than enough headroom. 203.0.113.0/16 is the right size, but that address space is a publicly routable documentation range rather than one of the RFC 1918 private ranges AWS recommends. A /30 netmask supplies only 4 addresses, nowhere near the 40,000 addresses of headroom the team needs.
